topics.concept: An LLM-as-judge grades model responses against a rubric, producing scores that approximate human preference at a fraction of the cost of human review. The simulation generates seeded response pairs with known quality gaps, then applies rubric-based scoring rules and calibration to measure agreement with ground truth. Key risks include positional bias and leniency that must be measured and corrected.
topics.data_idea: Creates seeded response sets with known quality tiers and injected judge biases, then scores them with the rubric engine to measure accuracy and bias rates.

key_params.bias_mode: positional or verbosity bias to inject

topics.name: LLM-as-Judge Evaluator
topics.real_world_use: Teams use judge models to score chat outputs during rapid iteration between human evaluations.

topics.concept: In a pairwise arena, judges pick the better of two model responses and Elo ratings update from wins and losses, exactly like chess rankings. The expected-score formula turns rating gaps into win probabilities, and the K-factor controls how fast ratings move. Seeded win histories let you verify the ratings converge on the true skill order.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded battles where each model has a hidden true skill, records judge votes with noise, and tracks Elo convergence toward the true ranking.
topics.name: Pairwise Elo Rating Arena
topics.real_world_use: Public model leaderboards rank chat models from thousands of blind human preference votes.

topics.concept: A good eval set covers the task space: difficulty tiers, edge cases, and categories the model must not regress on. This tool builds seeded question-answer sets with metadata tags, deduplicates near-identical items, and computes coverage stats over categories. Stratified sampling keeps small sets representative of the full distribution.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded QA items across categories with difficulty labels, dedupes them, and reports per-category coverage counts.
topics.name: Evaluation Dataset Builder
topics.real_world_use: Model teams curate internal golden datasets before every release to catch quality regressions.

topics.concept: Prompt changes can silently break previously correct outputs, so a regression suite re-runs a frozen set of prompts and compares new outputs against baselines. Semantic comparison catches meaning changes that string matching misses, and diff reports show exactly which cases regressed. A failing threshold gates deployment of the new prompt.
topics.data_idea: Builds a seeded frozen prompt set with baseline outputs, perturbs the prompt, and classifies each case as pass, regressed, or improved.
topics.name: Prompt Regression Test Suite
topics.real_world_use: Applied-AI teams gate prompt edits in CI before they reach production assistants.

topics.concept: A/B testing compares two prompts by splitting traffic and measuring a success metric, using a statistical test to decide whether the observed lift is real. Power analysis determines how many samples are needed, and early-stopping rules avoid peeking bias. Seeded simulations show how variance and effect size drive the required sample count.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded A/B runs with Bernoulli success outcomes under known true rates and records decisions, p-values, and stopping times.
topics.name: Prompt A/B Tester
topics.real_world_use: Product teams test prompt variants on live traffic before rolling out the winner.

topics.concept: Hallucinations are plausible statements that are unsupported or false. Detection strategies include checking claims against retrieved context, measuring self-consistency across multiple sampled answers, and scoring entity-level factuality. The simulation plants unsupported claims in generated text and measures detector precision and recall at claim granularity.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded answers mixing true and planted false claims over a synthetic fact base, then evaluates detector precision and recall.

key_params.hallucination_rate: fraction of claims that are fabricated

topics.name: Hallucination Detection Simulator
topics.real_world_use: RAG pipelines flag unsupported sentences before showing answers to users.

topics.concept: Groundedness measures how well an answer is supported by its source passages: each claim should be entailed by at least one passage. The scorer splits answers into atomic claims and runs entailment checks, producing a supported-claims ratio plus a list of orphan claims. This is the core metric for retrieval-augmented generation quality.
topics.data_idea: Synthesizes seeded passages and answers with labeled claim-to-passage mappings, then scores groundedness against the labels.

key_params.entailment_threshold: minimum entailment score to count as supported

topics.name: Groundedness Scorer
topics.real_world_use: Enterprise search assistants report groundedness to prove answers come from company documents.

topics.concept: ROUGE and BLEU score generated text by n-gram overlap with reference answers: ROUGE is recall-oriented for summarization, BLEU is precision-oriented with a brevity penalty for translation. They are fast and reproducible but blind to paraphrase quality, which is why modern evals pair them with semantic metrics. The suite implements them from scratch on tokenized text.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded reference texts and perturbed candidates (paraphrases, truncations, shuffles) and computes ROUGE and BLEU per pair.
topics.name: Text Overlap Metrics Suite
topics.real_world_use: Still the standard automatic metrics for summarization and translation benchmarks.

topics.concept: Semantic similarity judges whether two texts mean the same thing, using embedding vectors and cosine similarity instead of word overlap. It rewards good paraphrases that n-gram metrics punish, but it needs a threshold calibrated on labeled pairs and it can miss subtle negation flips. The simulation builds sentence embeddings from seeded random projections to demonstrate the geometry.
topics.data_idea: Creates seeded paraphrase and contradiction pairs with labels, embeds them, and measures threshold-based classification accuracy.
topics.name: Semantic Similarity Evaluator
topics.real_world_use: Semantic answer similarity is the backbone of modern LLM benchmark scoring.

topics.concept: Exact match is the strictest automatic grade: the normalized answer must equal a reference exactly. Normalization (lowercasing, article stripping, whitespace collapse) separates meaning from formatting noise. For math and extraction tasks it is reliable and cheap, but it unfairly fails valid alternative phrasings, so reports always pair it with a softer metric.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded QA pairs with answer aliases and formatting variants, then grades exact match with and without normalization.
topics.name: Exact Match Grading Engine
topics.real_world_use: Reading-comprehension and math benchmarks grade short answers with exact match.

topics.concept: Rubric grading decomposes quality into scored dimensions like accuracy, completeness, and tone, each with anchored scale descriptions. Dimension scores combine with weights into a final grade, and inter-rater agreement between rubric applications measures reliability. Structured rubrics make subjective judgments repeatable across runs and reviewers.
topics.data_idea: Scores seeded responses on a weighted rubric with noisy simulated raters and computes per-dimension means and agreement statistics.
topics.name: Rubric-Graded Evaluator
topics.real_world_use: Hiring and education platforms grade open-ended responses with rubric-based LLM judges.

topics.concept: A leaderboard aggregates scores across many evals into one comparable ranking, normalizing per-benchmark scales and handling missing entries gracefully. Confidence intervals around each score prevent overreading tiny gaps, and per-category breakdowns reveal strengths and weaknesses. The simulation replays seeded benchmark results into a live ranking table.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded per-benchmark scores with noise for each model and computes normalized aggregate rankings with confidence bands.
topics.name: Evaluation Leaderboard
topics.real_world_use: Open benchmark hubs publish aggregate leaderboards that teams watch for every model release.

topics.concept: Calibration asks whether a model's stated confidence matches its actual accuracy: a well-calibrated model is right 80 percent of the time it says 80 percent. Reliability diagrams bin predictions by confidence and plot accuracy per bin, and expected calibration error summarizes the gap. Temperature scaling is the classic post-hoc fix for overconfidence.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded predictions with known true probabilities and injected miscalibration, then computes reliability curves and ECE before and after scaling.
topics.name: Confidence Calibration Analyzer
topics.real_world_use: High-stakes classifiers in medicine and finance must be calibrated before deployment.

topics.concept: Automated judges carry systematic biases: preferring the first answer shown, favoring longer responses, or rewarding their own model's style. The detector runs swapped-position and length-controlled experiments to isolate each bias and reports effect sizes with significance. Counterbalancing presentation order is the standard mitigation the tests verify.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded judge decisions with injected positional and verbosity biases, then runs the detection tests and reports measured effect sizes.
topics.name: Judge Bias Detector
topics.real_world_use: Eval platforms audit their judges for positional bias before trusting leaderboard rankings.

topics.concept: A reliable model should give equivalent answers to paraphrased versions of the same question. The evaluator generates paraphrase variants of each prompt, collects answers, and measures semantic agreement across the set. Low consistency flags brittle reasoning even when the original answer scores well.
topics.data_idea: Builds seeded question sets with paraphrase variants and noisy answer mappings, then reports per-question consistency scores and outliers.
topics.name: Response Consistency Evaluator
topics.real_world_use: QA teams probe assistant reliability by rephrasing user queries across sessions.

topics.concept: Toxicity classifiers score text for harmful content across categories like insult, threat, and identity attack. Evaluation needs labeled edge cases because real harm is rare and ambiguous: precision matters more than recall when the classifier gates user-facing output. Threshold tuning trades false positives that censor legitimate speech against misses.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded texts with labeled toxicity categories including ambiguous edge cases, then computes precision, recall, and F1 across thresholds.
topics.name: Toxicity Scoring Simulator
topics.real_world_use: Social platforms and chat products gate generations with toxicity classifiers.

topics.concept: Latency benchmarks measure time to first token and tokens per second under controlled concurrency, because user-perceived speed depends on both. Percentile statistics (p50, p95, p99) matter more than means for SLOs, and warmup runs separate cold-start effects from steady state. The harness replays seeded request traces against a simulated server.
topics.data_idea: Synthesizes seeded request traces with varying prompt and output lengths, then simulates queueing and reports percentile latency stats.
topics.name: Inference Latency Benchmark
topics.real_world_use: Inference providers publish latency benchmarks to win serving contracts.

topics.concept: Every model choice trades quality against cost per token and latency. The analyzer plots the Pareto frontier across candidate models so teams can pick the cheapest model that clears a quality bar. Routing easy queries to small models and hard ones to large models beats any single model on the frontier.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded quality and cost points per model plus query difficulty labels, then computes the Pareto frontier and router savings.
topics.name: Cost-Quality Tradeoff Analyzer
topics.real_world_use: AI platforms route queries across model tiers to control inference spend.

topics.concept: Human evals remain the gold standard for open-ended quality: raters follow guidelines, overlapping assignments measure agreement, and adjudication resolves disputes. The workflow assigns items to raters, computes inter-rater agreement, and flags low-agreement items for guideline revision. Seeded rater noise models let you size the rater pool before spending.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded rater judgments with per-rater noise and bias, then computes agreement metrics and adjudication queues.
topics.name: Human Evaluation Workflow
topics.real_world_use: Model labs run human preference studies to validate every major release.

topics.concept: When a prompt changes, reviewers need to see exactly what changed in the outputs. The diff reviewer aligns old and new responses sentence by sentence, highlights additions, deletions, and meaning shifts, and groups cases by change severity. Reviewers approve or reject per case, building an audit trail for the prompt change.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded old and new response pairs with labeled change types and renders grouped diff summaries per severity band.
topics.name: Response Diff Reviewer
topics.real_world_use: Prompt engineers review output diffs before merging prompt changes.

topics.concept: A golden set is the frozen, hand-verified core of an eval suite that everything is measured against. The manager versions each item, tracks who approved it and when, and quarantines items that start failing for annotation review. Item retirement policies keep the set fresh as capabilities shift.
topics.data_idea: Maintains a seeded versioned item store with approval logs and simulates failure streaks to exercise quarantine and retirement rules.
topics.name: Golden Test Set Manager
topics.real_world_use: QA teams protect golden sets as the source of truth for release criteria.

topics.concept: Eval results only matter if stakeholders can read them: the report generator turns raw run JSON into summary tables, per-category breakdowns, significance notes, and trend charts against prior runs. Templated sections keep every report comparable, and a headline verdict answers whether the release bar was met.
topics.data_idea: Consumes seeded eval-run JSON with per-benchmark scores and renders a structured report with tables, deltas, and a verdict block.
topics.name: Evaluation Report Generator
topics.real_world_use: Release managers attach eval reports to every model launch decision.

topics.concept: Few-shot performance swings with the choice, order, and count of examples, sometimes by double digits. The probe sweeps example counts and permutations over a seeded task set and measures score variance, revealing whether a prompt is robust or lottery-like. Reporting the spread instead of a single number is the honest practice.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded task scores as a function of example count and order, then reports mean, spread, and the most stable configuration.
topics.name: Few-Shot Sensitivity Probe
topics.real_world_use: Researchers report few-shot variance to avoid cherry-picked benchmark numbers.

topics.concept: Long-context models are tested with needle-in-a-haystack retrieval: a fact is buried at varying depths in a long document and the model must find it. Performance typically degrades near the middle of the context, the lost-in-the-middle effect. The evaluator sweeps context length and needle depth to map the retrieval frontier.
topics.data_idea: Builds seeded long documents with facts inserted at controlled depths and simulates retrieval success as a function of length and depth.
topics.name: Long Context Evaluator
topics.real_world_use: Document-AI vendors prove retrieval quality across advertised context windows.
